title: Card Suit and Rank
story: You're building a poker game and need to model playing cards. Every card has a suit (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and a rank (Ace through King). A hand is 5 cards. You need to describe each card and check if two cards form a pair.
why: Two enums combined in one struct is the canonical card-deck pattern used in every card game.
analogy: A Card is a marriage of two independent choices: the suit (the symbol in the corner) and the rank (Ace through King). The deck is all 52 possible combinations. describe reads the card aloud like a dealer at a casino table.
try_it: Add a `Card.value(self) -> Int` method for blackjack (Ace=11, face=10, others=pip value). Create a full hand of 5 cards. Add a `has_flush(cards...) -> Bool` function that checks if all 5 cards share the same suit.
tips: Use two helper functions (rank_name, suit_name) instead of putting all logic inside describe
`a.rank == b.rank` compares the rank enum � enum variants support `==` comparison
Define enums before the struct that uses them � Suit and Rank must exist before Card references them
common_mistakes: Comparing cards with `a == b` to check for a pair � this only returns true if both suit AND rank match
Defining Card before Suit or Rank � the compiler reads top-to-bottom, so dependencies must come first
